design_detail: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4 (screening and diagnosis of perinatal mental health conditions); a priori protocol, librarian literature search, modified GRADE evidence-to-decision framework
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnant and postpartum individuals with mental health conditions
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no study sample
rationale: PubMed publication type is Practice Guideline; document issues graded recommendations on screening and diagnosis. Guidelines are code 12.

design_detail: Diagnostic manual (DSM-5-TR), American Psychiatric Association Publishing, 2022
comparison_group: None
population: General (psychiatric diagnostic criteria; not a study population)
sample_size_detail: Not a study; no sample
rationale: Citation is the DSM-5-TR; the protocol lists diagnostic manuals under 'Not a study (resource)'. File contains citation metadata only.

design_detail: Cross-sectional screening/prevalence study (self-described 'sequential case series'): telephone EPDS screening at 4-6 weeks postpartum with home SCID diagnostic interviews for screen-positive women, single urban academic hospital (Pittsburgh); descriptive statistics and chi-square/Fisher tests
severity_measure: Descriptive prevalence/diagnostic-yield study; no treatment or exposure comparison and no confounder adjustment
comparison_group: None (screen-positive vs screen-negative women compared descriptively)
population: Postpartum women who delivered at Magee-Womens Hospital, Pittsburgh, screened 4-6 weeks postpartum
sample_size_detail: 17426 eligible and agreed; 13442 contacted; 10000 screened; 1396 screen-positive (EPDS>=10); 826 completed home SCID visits and 147 telephone MDD interviews
rationale: Large screening study reporting proportions (onset timing, self-harm ideation, diagnoses) with only descriptive statistics and crude chi-square comparisons. Coded descriptive observational (code 5 precedes case series), although authors call it a 'sequential case series'.

design_detail: Website: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) page on perinatal mental health conditions (saferbirth.org patient safety bundle site)
comparison_group: None
population: Maternity care settings / perinatal patients (implementation resource)
sample_size_detail: Not a study; no sample
rationale: Citation is a web page accessed online and not indexed in PubMed; coded as a resource. URL path suggests a patient safety bundle, which could arguably be a consensus product, but the file has no content beyond the citation.

design_detail: Narrative clinical review of epidemiology, genetics, physiological triggers, diagnosis, treatment and prevention of postpartum psychosis
comparison_group: None
population: Women with postpartum psychosis/mania
sample_size_detail: Review; mentions individual studies (N=64 lithium; N=34 ECT) but no pooled sample
rationale: Authors 'reviewed' the research and summarized prior systematic reviews and sparse clinical studies; no systematic search or pooling described. PubMed type Review.

design_detail: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement (B recommendation) on depression screening in adults, based on evidence review
comparison_group: None
population: Adults aged 18 years and older, including pregnant and postpartum women
sample_size_detail: Recommendation statement; no study sample
rationale: USPSTF recommendation statement; PubMed type Practice Guideline. Applies to all adults including pregnant and postpartum women.

design_detail: American Academy of Pediatrics committee clinical report with practice and advocacy recommendations on perinatal depression in pediatric practice
comparison_group: None
population: Mothers with perinatal depression and their infants seen in pediatric medical homes
sample_size_detail: Clinical report; no study sample
rationale: Authored by an AAP committee and issues recommendations (e.g., PPD screening at 1-, 2-, 4-, 6-month visits). PubMed labels it Review, so narrative review is a plausible alternative.

design_detail: American College of Nurse-Midwives position statement (web PDF) on mental health during childbirth and across the lifespan
comparison_group: None
population: Childbearing people and women across the lifespan
sample_size_detail: Position statement; no study sample
rationale: Citation explicitly identifies the document as a 'Position statement', which the protocol places under code 12. Only citation metadata is available.

design_detail: Website of the National Curriculum in Reproductive Psychiatry (training program)
comparison_group: None
population: Clinicians/trainees in reproductive psychiatry
sample_size_detail: Not a study; no sample
rationale: Citation is a training-curriculum website (ncrptraining.org); the protocol lists training programs as resources.

design_detail: Systematic database search (MEDLINE, PreMEDLINE, Current Contents, Biological Abstracts, PsycINFO 1966-2002) and pooled analysis of published maternal plasma, breast-milk and infant plasma antidepressant levels in nursing mother-infant pairs
comparison_group: None (infant-to-maternal plasma ratios and correlations by drug)
population: Lactating mothers treated with antidepressants and their nursing infants
sample_size_detail: 57 studies included (67 identified); number of mother-infant pairs not reported in abstract
rationale: A pooled analysis of 57 studies found by electronic and bibliographic searches. Pooled analyses of multiple studies are code 7, which comes before PK (code 8), although the content is pharmacokinetic. Component studies are drug-level reports and case reports, none randomized.

design_detail: Narrative review and commentary on disparities in US suicide deaths, with presentation of publicly available CDC suicide data
comparison_group: None
population: US population (suicide deaths, 1999-2020)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; descriptive public data, no analytic study sample
rationale: Authors state 'this is not a systematic review' and describe it as part narrative review, part commentary.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of double-blind placebo-controlled antidepressant relapse-prevention trials identified by systematic literature search; odds ratios via Review Manager 5.0
comparison_group: Placebo (continuation antidepressant vs switch to placebo)
population: Patients with depressive disorders who responded to acute antidepressant treatment
sample_size_detail: 54 placebo-controlled relapse-prevention studies; patient n=9268
rationale: Meta-analysis of 54 double-blind placebo-controlled relapse-prevention studies (n=9268); PubMed type Meta-Analysis.

design_detail: Prospective cohort (subgroup with prior depressive disorder) recruited from 137 obstetric practices/clinics in Connecticut and western Massachusetts, 2005-2009; Cox regression with time-dependent, 2-month-lagged antidepressant use, unadjusted and adjusted
severity_measure: Number of lifetime depressive episodes before pregnancy (1/2/3/4+), depression onset before age 14, number of psychiatric hospitalizations for depression, major depressive episode in 6 months before pregnancy
comparison_group: Pregnant women with history of depression not using antidepressants (time-varying exposure)
population: Pregnant women with a history of depressive disorder, Connecticut and western Massachusetts, 2005-2009, followed to 2 months postpartum
sample_size_detail: Analytic sample 778 of 2793 interviewed; 130 used antidepressants during study period; 617 completed both follow-up interviews; 123 developed MDE
rationale: Adjusted Cox model includes prior episodes, early onset and psychiatric hospitalization, described as 'correlates of severe depressive illness', plus recent MDE. These are severity proxies under the protocol.

design_detail: PRISMA systematic review (MEDLINE, CENTRAL, EMBASE, Scopus to Dec 2019) and random-effects meta-analysis (Hedges g) of psychotherapy vs conventional obstetric care for antenatal depression, anxiety and quality of life
comparison_group: Conventional obstetric care
population: Pregnant women in the antenatal period
sample_size_detail: 22 studies: 17 RCTs and 5 controlled clinical trials; 2146 pregnant women
rationale: Self-described PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis. Results report 17 randomized controlled trials and 5 controlled clinical trials, so component designs are mixed.

design_detail: Joint American Psychiatric Association-ACOG work-group consensus report; non-systematic Medline/bibliography literature review with management algorithms for preconception and antenatal depression
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnant women and women planning pregnancy with depression
sample_size_detail: Consensus report; no study sample
rationale: Representatives of APA and ACOG reviewed literature and iterated drafts 'until consensus was achieved' to develop management algorithms. Coded as a consensus statement; narrative review (PubMed type Review) is an alternative.

design_detail: Clinical toolkit (Lifeline for Moms Perinatal Mental Health Toolkit, UMass Medical School, 2019); source for ACOG Figures 1 and 2
comparison_group: None
population: Perinatal patients and the obstetric clinicians caring for them
sample_size_detail: Not a study; no sample
rationale: Citation is a web-hosted clinical toolkit, not indexed in PubMed; coded as a resource.

design_detail: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of TCAs or SSRIs vs placebo for depression in primary care
comparison_group: Placebo
population: Adults under 65 years with depression recruited in primary care
sample_size_detail: 14 studies (16 comparisons); 1364 participants in intervention groups and 919 in placebo groups
rationale: Cochrane review including only randomised controlled trials of antidepressants vs placebo; 1364+919 participants.

design_detail: Rationale-and-design article for an investigation of pregnancy-associated SSRI pharmacokinetics and dosing in pregnant women with depression
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnant women with depression treated with SSRIs
sample_size_detail: Design paper; no results
rationale: Title states 'Rationale and design', and the abstract presents background only, with no results. Coded as protocol/design paper rather than PK because no data are reported.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Quebec health administrative databases (deliveries 1998-2002); multivariable log-binomial regression of miscarriage risk corrected for induced abortions; three comparison groups
severity_measure: Multivariable adjustment reported and comparison restricted to women with pre-pregnancy depression diagnosis (diagnosis only), but covariate list not available in abstract
comparison_group: Women with pre-pregnancy depression diagnosis and no first-trimester antidepressant; also nondepressed unexposed women and women using hypothyroid medication
population: Pregnant women delivering 1998-2002 identified in Quebec health administrative databases
sample_size_detail: Cohort of 41964 pregnant women; sizes of exposure/comparison groups not reported in abstract
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of antidepressant-exposed depressed women vs unexposed depressed women with multivariable regression. Restriction on diagnosis alone is not severity, and covariates are not listed, so severity is Unclear (coded excl. severity per Amendment 1(a)).

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (MOOSE; Embase, Medline, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Scopus to Dec 2012) of cohort and case-control studies of antidepressant exposure and PPHN
comparison_group: Infants of pregnant women unexposed to the antidepressant under study
population: Pregnant women and their newborns
sample_size_detail: 7 studies (5 cohort, 2 case-control); 5 pooled for late-pregnancy SSRI exposure; total participants not reported
rationale: Self-described systematic review and meta-analysis restricted to cohort and case-control studies; no pooled participant total reported.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of cohort and case-control studies of maternal SSRI use and PPHN (PubMed, Medline, EMBASE, Web of Science, Google Scholar, 1960-2017)
comparison_group: Infants of mothers without SSRI use in pregnancy
population: Pregnant women and their liveborn infants
sample_size_detail: 9 cohort and case-control studies reviewed (8 meta-analyzed), 7540265 subjects in total
rationale: Updated meta-analysis of 9 cohort and case-control studies, 7,540,265 subjects; PubMed type Meta-Analysis.

design_detail: Secondary analysis of 2 NIMH-funded prospective observational cohort studies (Cleveland and Pittsburgh, 2000-2011); blinded Finnegan Scale exam at 2-4 weeks; chi-square/Kruskal-Wallis comparisons plus multivariable logistic regression
severity_measure: Logistic model adjusted only for preterm birth, maternal race and age; groups defined by mood-disorder diagnosis; SIGH-ADS depression scores compared descriptively but not included in outcome model
comparison_group: Infants of women with mood disorder unexposed to psychotropics (n=94) and of healthy unexposed women (n=79)
population: Pregnant women with MDD or bipolar disorder (SRI-treated or untreated) or no mood disorder, and their infants, Cleveland and Pittsburgh, 2000-2011
sample_size_detail: SRI-exposed 41, mood disorder unexposed 94, comparison 79
rationale: Main reported comparison is crude (chi-square), with a confounder-adjusted logistic regression (preterm, race, age) reported as 'results not shown'. No severity measure was adjusted for. Unadjusted/descriptive is a plausible alternative code.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO to June 2010) of cohort and case-control studies of prenatal antidepressant exposure and poor neonatal adaptation syndrome, respiratory distress and tremors
comparison_group: Infants not exposed to antidepressants in utero
population: Pregnant women and their newborns
sample_size_detail: 12 studies included; pooled participant total not reported in abstract
rationale: Self-described systematic review and meta-analysis restricted to cohort and case-control studies; PubMed types Meta-Analysis and Systematic Review.

design_detail: Systematic literature review (MEDLINE 1966-2005, PsycINFO, FDA advisory data) with Mantel-Haenszel summary risk ratio from cohort studies and summary of case reports on neonatal signs after late SRI exposure
comparison_group: Early-gestation SRI exposure or no exposure
population: Neonates exposed to SRIs in the last trimester through delivery
sample_size_detail: 9 cohort studies and 13 case reports (18 cases); pooled participant total not reported
rationale: Titled a literature review, but reports database searches, explicit inclusion criteria and a pooled Mantel-Haenszel risk ratio, which fits code 7. Component studies are cohort studies and case reports.

design_detail: Register-based cohort, Swedish Medical Birth Register; infants of mothers reporting benzodiazepine/hypnotic BZRA use in early pregnancy (or prescribed in late pregnancy) vs all births; adjusted ORs
severity_measure: Adjusted ORs reported but covariates not listed in abstract; comparison is all births with no restriction on indication
comparison_group: All births in the Swedish Medical Birth Register (general population)
population: Infants born in Sweden to mothers using benzodiazepines/hypnotic benzodiazepine receptor agonists during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 1979 infants (1944 mothers) exposed in early pregnancy; 401 infants (390 mothers) exposed in late pregnancy; compared with all births (n=873879)
rationale: Non-randomized register comparison reporting an adjusted OR for malformations. Covariates are unavailable, so severity is Unclear (coded excl. severity per Amendment 1(a)); comparator is all births, not people with the indication.

design_detail: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 187 on neural tube defects
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnancies affected by or at risk for fetal neural tube defects
sample_size_detail: Practice bulletin; no study sample
rationale: ACOG Practice Bulletin; PubMed type Practice Guideline, which the protocol places under code 12.

design_detail: Narrative review (Current Opinion 'purpose of review' format) of animal and clinical evidence on high-dose folic acid to prevent congenital heart defects
comparison_group: None
population: Women before and in early pregnancy (with extrapolation from animal studies)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no study sample
rationale: Non-systematic opinion review summarizing animal and clinical findings, with no search methods described. PubMed type Review.

design_detail: Pooled reanalysis of individual data from five prospective European cohort studies of antiepileptic drug exposure in pregnancy and major congenital malformations
comparison_group: Matched nonepileptic unexposed control pregnancies (n=158); also comparisons across AED regimens and valproate doses
population: Children of mothers with epilepsy exposed to AEDs in utero, and unexposed control children, from 5 European prospective studies
sample_size_detail: 1221 AED-exposed and 158 unexposed control children; main exposed-vs-control comparison used 192 exposed vs 158 matched controls
rationale: Data from five prospective studies were 'pooled and reanalyzed'. Pooled/IPD analyses of multiple studies are code 7 (PubMed type Meta-Analysis), although the analysis resembles a pooled cohort.

design_detail: Prospective pharmacokinetic study of carbamazepine and its 10,11-epoxide/diol metabolites in maternal serum, urine and amniotic fluid in early pregnancy; relation to dose, comedication and pregnancy outcome
comparison_group: Pregnancies with normal vs malformed outcome (unadjusted comparison of drug/metabolite levels)
population: Pregnant women with epilepsy taking carbamazepine in the first trimester, referred for prenatal diagnosis before 16 weeks
sample_size_detail: 100 pregnancies with first-trimester CBZ exposure, 7 with malformed outcome
rationale: Measures drug and metabolite concentrations and their determinants. The outcome comparison is limited to unadjusted level differences, which fits code 8.

design_detail: Single case report of a neonate with fatal cardiac malformation attributed to maternal valproate use (fetal valproate syndrome)
comparison_group: None
population: Neonate exposed to valproate in utero
sample_size_detail: One neonate
rationale: PubMed type Case Reports; abstract describes one neonate.

design_detail: Clinical case series of 19 children exposed to valproic acid in utero, evaluated for fetal valproate syndrome features, with literature comparison
comparison_group: None (VPA monotherapy vs VPA plus other anticonvulsants described within series; no unexposed group)
population: Children exposed to valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: 19 exposed children evaluated
rationale: Exposed children described without an unexposed comparison group; PubMed types Case Reports and Review.

design_detail: Case series of 28 valproate-exposed infants identified through the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC), 1976-1988, combined with published cases and epidemiologic data
comparison_group: None (VPA monotherapy vs VPA plus other anticonvulsants described; no unexposed group)
population: Infants prenatally exposed to valproic acid, Spain
sample_size_detail: 28 exposed cases: 15 VPA monotherapy, 13 VPA plus other anticonvulsants
rationale: Describes clinical manifestations in 28 exposed cases, supplemented by a literature review, with no unexposed comparison group. The epidemiologic discussion is secondary.

design_detail: Letter/comment reporting case(s) of fetal valproate syndrome with autism (per PubMed publication types); no abstract available
comparison_group: None
population: Children with fetal valproate syndrome and autism (from title)
sample_size_detail: Number of cases not determinable (no abstract in file)
rationale: PubMed publication types are Case Reports, Comment and Letter, with no abstract. Coded case report (code 9 precedes commentary). evidence_basis set to citation_only because the file has metadata only, although the batch listed abstract_only.

design_detail: Case series of five patients with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
comparison_group: None
population: Children with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
sample_size_detail: Five additional patients (a previously reported patient is referenced but not counted)
rationale: Abstract presents five patients with FVS and autism; no comparison group.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort via postal questionnaire to women aged 16-40 at the Mersey Regional Epilepsy Clinic (UK); odds ratios for additional educational needs by in utero AED exposure (monotherapy, polytherapy, valproate, carbamazepine)
severity_measure: Abstract reports odds ratios without mention of adjustment; covariates (including any epilepsy severity/seizure measures) not described
comparison_group: School-age children of mothers with epilepsy not exposed to AEDs in utero (n=176)
population: School-age children (4-18 years) of women with epilepsy registered at the Mersey Regional Epilepsy Clinic, UK
sample_size_detail: 1267 women approached, 721 returned questionnaires, 330 had live births; 594 children, 400 school-age (150 monotherapy, 74 polytherapy, 176 unexposed)
rationale: Exposed and unexposed children compared with ORs, and the abstract never says whether they are adjusted, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear and Low confidence per Amendment 1(b). The survey format is a data-collection method rather than a code 10 design, because comparative effect estimates are reported.

design_detail: Narrative review of valproic acid teratogenicity, prenatal diagnosis and counseling for psychiatric patients of reproductive age
comparison_group: None
population: Women of reproductive age treated with valproic acid for bipolar/affective disorders
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no study sample
rationale: Clinical overview with recommendations and no search methods described; PubMed type Review.

design_detail: Prospective case series of 22 term infants exposed in utero to valproate (20 monotherapy, 2 with carbamazepine); hypoglycaemia and withdrawal symptoms described and correlated with maternal valproate dose/plasma concentrations
comparison_group: None described in abstract (no unexposed group)
population: Term infants of women with epilepsy treated with valproate during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 22 mother-infant pairs (20 VPA only, 2 VPA plus carbamazepine); 13 hypoglycaemic, 10 with withdrawal symptoms
rationale: Single-arm prospective series of exposed infants with no comparison group described. It includes correlations with maternal plasma valproate (PK elements), but the primary aim is describing clinical outcomes, so coded case series rather than PK.

design_detail: Review with stated multi-database search (MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, 1996 onward, any language) of reports of gestational diabetes with second-generation antipsychotic exposure; qualitative synthesis with expert opinion, no pooling
comparison_group: None (case counts of GDM by SGA)
population: Pregnant women exposed to second-generation antipsychotics
sample_size_detail: Number of included studies not reported; 18 GDM cases identified across reports
rationale: Describes a defined search of four databases with explicit inclusion and no limits on method or language, so coded systematic review. However, PubMed lists only Review and the article is an Expert Opinion piece, so narrative review is a strong alternative. Sources are case reports and retrospective/prospective studies.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract (MAX) 2000-2007; three levels of analysis (unadjusted; restricted to women with depression; depression-restricted with propensity-score stratification in 100 strata); high-dimensional PS confirmatory analysis
severity_measure: Number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses (explicit depression-severity proxies) in the propensity score, plus other psychotropic medications and other antidepressant indications
comparison_group: Women with a depression diagnosis not exposed to antidepressants in the first trimester
population: Pregnant women enrolled in US Medicaid (MAX, 46 states + DC) with liveborn infants, 2000-2007
sample_size_detail: Full cohort 949504 pregnancies (64389 antidepressant-exposed, 885115 unexposed); fully adjusted depression-restricted SSRI analysis 36778 SSRI-exposed vs 180564 unexposed (217342)
rationale: Primary fully adjusted analysis restricts to depression and uses PS stratification including 'proxies for depression severity'. Study type and severity coding are clear. Confidence is Medium only because N could be the full cohort (949504) or the depression-restricted analytic set.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000-2007, restricted to women with depression diagnoses; GEE relative risks adjusted for delivery year, preeclampsia risk factors, depression-severity proxies, other indications, psychotropics and utilization; hdPS and other sensitivity analyses
severity_measure: Number of outpatient (0, 1, 2-4, 5-9, >=10) and inpatient (0, 1, >=2) depression diagnoses, explicitly labeled depression-severity proxies
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression and no antidepressant dispensed (n=59219); SSRI monotherapy as active comparator in secondary analysis
population: Pregnant women with depression diagnoses enrolled in US Medicaid (MAX), 2000-2007
sample_size_detail: 100942 women with depression; 15175 first-trimester-only antidepressant users excluded from primary analysis; 59219 unexposed, 19000 SSRI, 1216 SNRI, 441 TCA, 2622 bupropion, 647 other, 2622 polytherapy (paper labels units as women; GEE accounts for multiple pregnancies)
rationale: Restricted to depression and adjusted for numbers of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses, described as 'proxies of depression severity'. Analytic N summed from Table 2 groups.

design_detail: Population-based prospective birth cohort using Finnish national registers (singleton live births 1996-2010); SSRI-exposed vs psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed vs medication- and diagnosis-free pregnancies; odds ratios
severity_measure: Comparison group restricted on presence of psychiatric diagnoses (not severity); abstract does not state covariates or explicitly describe adjustment
comparison_group: Pregnancies unexposed to SSRIs but with psychiatric diagnoses (n=9652); also pregnancies unexposed to medications and psychiatric diagnoses (n=31394)
population: Singleton live births in Finland, 1996-2010 (national register data)
sample_size_detail: Sampling frame 845345 offspring; analytic groups 15729 SSRI-exposed, 9652 psychiatric unexposed, 31394 unexposed
rationale: Register comparison designed to account for psychiatric diagnoses through the comparison group. The abstract reports ORs but never says whether they are adjusted, so per Amendment 1(b) it is coded unadjusted/descriptive with severity Unclear and Low confidence.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of neonatal outcomes and poor neonatal adaptation after in utero exposure to serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants
comparison_group: Unexposed infants, including infants of mothers diagnosed with depression
population: Neonates exposed in utero to SRI antidepressants
sample_size_detail: 33 relevant studies (69 outcomes; 17 outcomes meta-analyzed); pooled participants not reported
rationale: Self-described systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies. The abstract does not state the component designs.
